## History

Bertha Shirley was deeply in love with her husband when they were married, but she died while her daughter [Anne](../character/anne.md) was still a young child. Years after her death, a packet of her old love letters was preserved by the current owner of her former home in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke). When [Anne](../character/anne.md) visited her parents' graves and received the letters, her daughter finally felt a deep, personal connection to Bertha and her husband.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P1](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P3](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER V. ## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--bertha-shirley.md)

Bertha Shirley was the biological mother of [Anne](../character/anne.md), though she died when [Anne](../character/anne.md) was an infant. [Anne](../character/anne.md) grew up knowing very little about her parents, but later in her youth she visited her childhood home in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke) and received a packet of old love letters written by Bertha and her husband. Reading these letters allowed [Anne](../character/anne.md) to finally feel a deep, personal connection to her mother.

- Parent of  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v3 ch.Yesterday P20](../source/v03-c21.md#nw-v03-c21-p0020)</sub>
